nodes.name: Email Trigger (IMAP)
nodes.notes: Trigger every time receives an email

categories.description: Emails that express strong intent or buying signals. These usually include direct questions about product samples, pricing, availability, or logistical steps like providing a shipping address. The sender appears decision-ready or is actively evaluating gloves for purchase. Examples of signals:  Asking for price, samples, MOQ  “Can you send me X?”  “Our address is...”  “We are looking to purchase gloves…

Mildly interested responses that are not direct buying signals. These may express general curiosity, requests for more information, or soft engagement. Often vague or non-committal. Examples of signals:  “Send me more details.”  “I’ll pass this to my manager.”  “We might be interested.”  “What do you offer?”

Messages where the recipient redirects you to someone else in the organization or provides an alternative contact person. Often includes names, emails, or roles. Examples of signals:  “You should speak to John.”  “I’m not the right contact, but here’s who is…”  “Forwarding this to our purchasing team.”

Clear rejection or opt-out messages. These may include requests to be removed, mention of an existing supplier, or a statement that they are not currently using gloves. Examples of signals:  “Please remove me from your list.”  “We already have a supplier.”  “We don’t use gloves.”
Automatic replies indicating the recipient is unavailable, on vacation, or no longer with the company. Examples of signals: “I’m currently out of office…”  “This mailbox is no longer monitored…”

Irrelevant, unsolicited, or clearly off-topic emails that do not require a reply. May include mass marketing, promotional offers, or completely unrelated content. Examples of signals:  Promotions from unrelated vendors  Random newsletters  Messages with no clear connection to glove sales

parameters.text:
=Read the automatic reply below. The contact is away or no longer at the company.

If there is a new contact name or email, extract it and note it for future outreach.
Do not write a reply unless a new contact is explicitly provided — then thank them or acknowledge transition.

Email: {{ $('Email Trigger (IMAP)').item.json.textPlain }}

Reference Templates:

1. Hi [New Contact’s Name],
I was informed via [Previous Contact's Name]’s auto-reply that you're now the appropriate person to speak with regarding glove supplies.

I'd be happy to support you with samples or pricing information, depending on your needs.
To get started, could you please let me know:

What type of gloves you're currently using?

Approximate monthly usage (in cases)?

Preferred shipping address (if you'd like samples)?

Looking forward to connecting and assisting you.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

2. Hi [Name],
Thanks for your auto-reply. I understand you're currently out of office until [Return Date] — no problem at all.

I’ll follow up after you’re back to check in again. In the meantime, if someone else is covering your responsibilities and you'd prefer I reach out to them, just let me know.

Wishing you a restful break,
[Your Name]

3. Hi [New Contact’s Name],
I understand that [Previous Contact’s Name] is no longer with the company and that you've taken over their responsibilities.

If gloves are still relevant for your team, I'd be happy to support you with samples or pricing to compare with your current provider.
Let me know if you'd be open to a quick conversation or want samples sent your way.

Looking forward to working together,
[Your Name]

4. Hi [Team],
I received an auto-reply from [Name] indicating they’re currently unavailable.

If someone else on your team is handling glove supplies in their absence, I'd appreciate it if you could point me in the right direction or forward this message to them.

Thanks for your help, and I hope [Name] has a smooth return.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

5. Hi [New Contact’s Name],
I was forwarded to you as the temporary contact while [Previous Contact's Name] is away.

I'm reaching out regarding gloves — we’re supporting facilities like yours with free samples and competitive pricing options.
Please let me know if this is something you're involved with, or if there’s someone else I should connect with during this period.

Appreciate your time,
[Your Name]

parameters.text:
=Read the email below. Based on its content:
1. Glove type (Nitrile, Latex, Vinyl)
2. Glove thickness (Light, Medium, Heavy-duty)
3. Monthly usage in cases

Then, write a professional reply do not mention the subject in the email body. Always Include the estimate:

Rules for providing Estimation:

1. Glove Type Estimation:
Estimated based on industry and customer role.
Industry / Role - Likely Glove Type(s)
i- Food processing / produce / meat - Nitrile (blue, sometimes black)
ii- Medical / clinics / testing - Nitrile (blue, exam grade)
iii- Law enforcement / prisons / EMS - Nitrile (black, fentanyl-resistant)
iv- Janitorial / cleaning services - Nitrile or latex (often powder-free)
v- Automotive / mechanical - Nitrile (black or orange, industrial)
vi- Tattoo / beauty / salons - Nitrile (black or purple)
vii- Education (custodial / food) - Nitrile or vinyl (blue/clear)
viii- Farming / agriculture (harvesters) - Nitrile or latex (blue, green, white)

2. Thickness Estimation
Based on job role or use-case.
Use Case / Job Role - Thickness (in mils)
i- Food handling / prep - 3–4 mil
ii- Medical exam / clinics - 4–5 mil
iii- Custodial / light cleaning - 4–5 mil
iv- Law enforcement / corrections - 6–8 mil
v- Automotive / heavy-duty - 6–8 mil
vi- Tattoo / salons - 4–6 mil
vii- Janitorial with chemicals - 5–6 mil minimum

3. Monthly Usage Estimation
Estimated by company size and facility type.
Company Type - Staff Size - Estimated Monthly Usage
i- Small food biz (1 site) - <20 staff - 1–3 cases
ii- Medium plant or clinic - 20–50 staff - 4–10 cases
iii- Multi-site / regional ops - 50–200 staff - 10–50+ cases
iv- Enterprise (multi-state) - 200+ staff - 50–500+ cases

Ask these 3 questions in this order (If, glove type thickness, and monthly usage is not provided:
1. Roughly how many cases do you go through per month?
2. What thickness do you prefer?
3. What type of gloves do you use?

Email:  {{ $('Email Trigger (IMAP)').item.json.textPlain }}

Reference Templates:

1. Hi Michelle — thanks so much for looping in Greg and Chelsea!

Hi Greg, hi Chelsea — great to meet you both. We’re preparing a sample shipment of nitrile gloves for your team, and I just want to make sure we send the right type for your environment.

Based on your operation, we estimate your team may be using medium-duty nitrile gloves, likely in the 4–6 mil range, with monthly usage somewhere between 5–10 cases, depending on roles and departments. 

To be sure, could you confirm a few quick details?

Roughly how many cases do you go through per month?
What thickness do you prefer? (Light, Medium, Heavy-duty, or in mils)
What type of gloves do you use most? (Nitrile, Latex, Vinyl)
 
Once I hear back, I’ll ship out the most relevant samples for your team to try.
Best regards,
[Your Name]

2. Hi Phillip,

Roughly how many cases do you go through per month?

Once we have this info, I’ll make sure we send the right match to your Lumberton facility.

Looking forward to your response.

Best regards,
Jessica
Acme Supply

We’ll use this info to fine-tune the sample selection and discuss pricing options if you're interested.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

5. Hi [Name],
I was referred to you as the person overseeing glove purchasing for your team. Based on the industry and use-case, we estimate you may go through around 10–15 cases/month of medium-duty nitrile gloves.

We’d be glad to send you some sample options to compare quality and fit — free of charge, including shipping.

To get started, could you let me know:

How many cases of gloves do you use monthly?

Thanks again — looking forward to assisting you.

Best regards,
[Your Name]
